lessons.title: Tashahhud · testimony
lessons.arabic: التَّحِيَّاتُ لِلَّهِ، وَالصَّلَوَاتُ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْكَ أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، السَّلاَمُ عَلَيْنَا وَعَلَى عِبَادِ اللَّهِ الصَّالِحِينَ، أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ اللَّهُ، وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ
lessons.meaning: Greetings, prayers, and good things belong to Allah. Peace, Allah’s mercy, and His blessings be upon you, Prophet. Peace be upon us and Allah’s righteous servants. I testify that none is worthy of worship except Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger.
lessons.question: How is Muhammad ﷺ described at the end of this wording?
lessons.note: This lesson follows the wording in the cited Ibn Masud report. The short Roman guide covers the opening only. Other authentic tashahhud wordings are also narrated, including Muslim 403a.

lessons.title: Sending blessings
lessons.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا صَلَّيْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ، اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ، وَعَلَى آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ، كَمَا بَارَكْتَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ، وَعَلَى آلِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، إِنَّكَ حَمِيدٌ مَجِيدٌ
lessons.meaning: O Allah, bestow prayers upon Muhammad and his family as You bestowed prayers upon Ibrahim and his family. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and his family as You blessed Ibrahim and his family. You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.
lessons.transliteration: Allahumma salli ala Muhammadin wa ala ali Muhammad…
lessons.question: Which earlier prophet is named?
lessons.note: The Roman guide covers the opening only. Read the full Arabic wording and its source; other narrated forms also exist.

lessons.title: The closing greeting
lessons.meaning: Peace and Allah’s mercy be upon you.

methodology: Fifteen lessons cover seven Al-Fatiha ayahs and selected hadith-based recitations from opening to closing. Quran wording is canonical Arabic with Pickthall English. Non-Quran meanings are original concise renderings of the cited ancient Arabic, with approximate Roman reading aids where provided. This is a guide to meanings, not a complete legal prayer manual. The licensed local Al-Fatiha recording plays the full surah; audio for the other recitations is not included.
